scenario.question: Resolve the eight triggers on the stack. With Torbran's replacement effect applied, how much damage does EACH opponent take from Brallin's seven triggers, how much does opponent 1 take from Spider-Man's single trigger, and what life total is each of the three opponents left on?

steps.action: Confirm the stack as given: Windfall has resolved and you discarded seven cards. Brallin's 'whenever you discard a card' triggered seven times (once per card) and Spider-Man's 'whenever you discard one or more cards' triggered once for the batch; all eight were put on the stack the next time you would receive priority, in the order you chose — Spider-Man's at the bottom (pos 0), the seven Brallin triggers above it. No player responds, so all players pass and the top object resolves first.
steps.effect: Eight triggered abilities on the stack, all controlled by you: Spider-Man's trigger (7 damage, targeting opponent 1) at pos 0, Brallin triggers 1-7 at pos 1-7. Brallin's trigger 7 of 7 (pos 7, the last added) is the first to resolve. Opponents: 40 / 40 / 40.

citations.quote: An ability triggers only once each time its trigger event occurs. However, it can trigger repeatedly if one event contains multiple occurrences.
Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.
puts each triggered ability they control with a trigger condition that isn’t another ability triggering on the stack in any order they choose
When all players pass in succession, the top (last-added) spell or ability on the stack resolves.

steps.action: Brallin, Skyshark Rider's triggered ability (7 of 7) resolves: put a +1/+1 counter on Brallin, then Brallin deals 1 damage to each opponent.
steps.effect: Brallin becomes 4/4 (one +1/+1 counter). The damage is dealt by Brallin, a red source you control, to each opponent; Torbran's 'deals that much damage plus 2 instead' is a replacement effect that modifies each opponent's damage event as it would happen, so Brallin deals 3 damage to each opponent instead of 1. Each opponent loses 3 life. The counter does not change the damage: the ability says 'deals 1 damage', not 'damage equal to its power'. Official rulings agree: Torbran's extra 2 is dealt by the same source as the original damage (here Brallin, not Torbran), and Brallin gets exactly one counter per resolution no matter how many opponents are dealt damage. Opponents: 37 / 37 / 37.

citations.quote: The controller of the spell or ability follows its instructions in the order written. However, replacement effects may modify these actions.
A +X/+Y counter on a creature or on a creature card in a zone other than the battlefield, where X and Y are numbers, adds X to that object’s power and Y to that object’s toughness.
Damage may be dealt as an effect of a spell or ability. The spell or ability will specify which object deals that damage.
Effects that use the word “instead” are replacement effects.

replacement effects apply continuously as events happen—they aren’t locked in ahead of time. Such effects watch for a particular event that would happen and completely or partially replace that event with a different event.
Damage dealt to a player by a source without infect causes that player to lose that much life.

steps.action: After each trigger resolves, you (the active player) would receive priority; the game checks state-based actions first. This repeats after every one of the eight resolutions in this scenario.
steps.effect: No opponent is at 0 or less life at any point during the seven Brallin triggers (lowest reached is 19), so no player loses the game. No new abilities trigger on the damage. Brallin is one of your commanders, but every point it deals here is noncombat damage from its triggered ability, so the commander-damage state-based action — which counts only combat damage dealt by the same commander — is not met at any point, including when the running total from Brallin reaches 21 per opponent. You receive priority, all players pass again, and the next-topmost Brallin trigger resolves. Steps 4-9 each end with this same check.

final_state.summary: Brallin's seven triggers each dealt 1 + 2 = 3 damage to each opponent (Torbran's replacement effect applied to every separate damage event from a red source): 21 damage to EACH opponent, 63 across the pod. Spider-Man's single trigger dealt 7 + 2 = 9 damage to opponent 1 only. Final life totals: opponent 1 at 10 (40 - 21 - 9), opponent 2 at 19 (40 - 21), opponent 3 at 19 (40 - 21). scope_notes: Scenario-facts agrees with the scenario prose on every figure used: 3 opponents at 40, 3 creature bodies, nothing sacrificed to pay a cost. It flags Torbran and Spider-Man as NOT in the sleeved 99; they are on the torbran-v1 branch (oracle text read from data/decks/sharknado/branches/torbran-v1/cards.json), as the scenario's own assumption states.

Rulings read as input: Torbran (the extra 2 is dealt by the original source; a damage-modifying effect's order is the damaged player's choice — no other such effect exists here), Brallin (one counter per resolution; damage dealt even if the counter can't be placed). Spider-Man and Windfall have no official rulings. No ruling is cited.
Out of scope by instruction: Windfall's resolution, combat, counters-as-power, and the draw.

findings.note: Windfall's discard is one event with seven occurrences of 'you discard a card' (the rule's own example: one spell destroying all lands triggers once per land); Spider-Man's 'one or more cards' condition occurs once. Seven Brallin triggers, one Spider-Man trigger.

Triggers go on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, i.e. after Windfall finishes resolving. Agrees with the Brallin ruling of 2020-04-17 ('that spell or ability finishes resolving before Brallin's triggered ability does').

All eight abilities have trigger conditions that are not 'another ability triggering', so all fall in the first part of the two-part process and you order them as you choose. Fragment quote; the surrounding text does not change its meaning here.
Top (last-added) object resolves when all pass; pos 7 (Brallin 7 of 7) first, Spider-Man at pos 0 last.
Instructions in written order (counter, then damage) and 'replacement effects may modify these actions'.
3/3 -> 4/4 from one +1/+1 counter; the rule's scope (power/toughness only) is what leaves the fixed '1 damage' in the ability text untouched.

'it deals 1 damage' names Brallin as the source; Brallin is red (cards.json colors ['R']), so Torbran's 'red source you control' condition is met. Agrees with the Torbran ruling of 2019-10-04 that the extra 2 is dealt by the original source.
Torbran's text uses 'instead'; it is a replacement effect.

'apply continuously as events happen — they aren't locked in ahead of time' makes Torbran apply to each separate damage event rather than once. Per-opponent application inside one resolution follows from Torbran's own condition ('would deal damage to AN opponent') meeting three separate recipients; agrees with the 2019-10-04 ruling that divided/assigned damage is modified per recipient after division. No second replacement or prevention effect is on this board, so 616.1 ordering never arises.
Neither Brallin nor Spider-Man has infect; 3 damage = 3 life lost. 40 -> 37 checks.
Active player receives priority after each ability resolves.

SBA check before priority, repeated after every resolution. With 704.6c now walked, the listed conditions that could bite on this board (704.5a life, 704.6c commander damage; 704.5j legend rule has one copy of each legend) are all accounted for.
No opponent is at 0 or less at any point (minimum 19 during the Brallin triggers).

Iteration-1 finding addressed. Full rule: 'In a Commander game, a player who's been dealt 21 or more combat damage by the same commander over the course of the game loses the game.' Brallin is one of sharknado's two commanders (decklist.txt Commander block), its running total reaches exactly 21 per opponent, and every point is noncombat damage from a triggered ability; the prose says so and the quote carries the operative words 'combat damage'. The quote drops the leading 'In a Commander game,' but the prose frames it as the commander-damage SBA, so it is not out of context.
37 -> 34. The 'deals 3 instead of 1' claim in this step is carried by reference to step 2's 614.1, not by 120.3a itself; acceptable since step 2 is explicit.
22 -> 19. Brallin 3/3 + seven counters = 10/10 checks.
Target legality re-checked on resolution; opponent 1 is in the same zone and still an opponent.

'Spider-Man deals that much damage' names Spider-Man as the source; Spider-Man is red (torbran-v1 cards.json colors ['R']). 'That much' = 7 is the ability text read against the single trigger event of seven discards (603.2c, step 1).
One damage event of 7 to one opponent -> 9 instead. Opponents 2 and 3 are not dealt damage by this ability.
19 -> 10 for opponent 1.
Final SBA check with an empty stack; 704.5a and 704.6c both walked.
10 / 19 / 19, none at 0 or less; nobody loses on life.
Same as step 3: exactly 21 from a commander, all noncombat, so the SBA is not met; the prose states the reason with the rule's operative words.
